text:
megan: Seeing a cluster of OOMs on prod for AWQ-quantized models this morning. Starts when traffic spikes and we get ~8 concurrent streams. logs show kv cache dtype upcast and a bunch of transient allocations. :frowning:

kai: Ugh. Any repro on staging? Which allocator path is firing?

megan: Repro on staging with loadtest-3. Attached profiler snapshot (summary): sudden 600MB workspace growth in the first 100ms of request handling, then a deferred-free spike. Kernel selector chooses fp16->fp32 path for a few layers.

anil: Can you paste the relevant trace? Also which batching heuristic was used (latency vs throughput)?

megan: Latency-first. Trace snippet:```
[ALLOC] slabpool: allocate 786432000 bytes for kv-cache-upcast
[kernel] select: matmul_fused_fp16->fp32_fallback (score 0.72)
[FREE-DEFER] mark for free at next safe point
[OOM] failed to reserve 256MB for temporary GEMM workspace
```

kai: Looks like two things colliding: (1) KV cache dtype upcast from AWQ->fp16/32 path allocating big transient buffers, (2) batch hint/continuous batching causing many in-flight prefix caches.

sre_oncall: We had alerts for the same hosts. Repro note: warmup traffic reduces incidence. Cold-start packing seems to fragment the slab.

anil: Hypothesis: our deferred-free window is too long for latency-first workloads with AWQ. We keep transient workspaces until end-of-request which overlaps multiple requests.

megan: Proposed quick mitigations: reduce deferred-free window, enable eager compact for small transient buffers, and add a coldstart compact pass when concurrency goes above threshold.

kai: Also consider making kv cache dtype per-request policy: keep AWQ dtype (uint8/packed) in KV cache and only upcast on-demand in kernel when needed — avoids large global scratch allocations.

anil: Agree. We should test a 'lazy-upcast' flag: only allocate scratch at per-layer execution time and free immediately after. Might increase peak CPU ops but reduce GPU mem churn.

sre_oncall: For immediate rollout, can we flip an autoscaling knob to shed latency-first routes toward lower-concurrency nodes?

megan: We already have a routing policy but traffic peaks hit all regions. Prefer code fixes first. Adding a temporary per-node guard to reject >6 concurrent streams for the AWQ model until we patch. :+1:

kai: For experiments, I'll add two profiling builds: one with deferred-free-window reduced to 32ms and eager compact enabled, another with lazy-upcast. We'll run batch of 1000 synthetic chats with variable prefix lengths.

megan: Config snippets for the test (put in staging pipeline):```json
{
  "allocator": {
    "deferred_free_window_ms": 32,
    "eager_compact_threshold": 131072,
    "enable_coldstart_compact": true
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "preserve_awq_packed": true,
    "lazy_upcast": true
  },
  "batching": {
    "max_inflight_streams": 6,
    "mode": "latency"
  }
}
```

anil: Nice. Add a perf counter for "transient_scratch_peak" and "kv_upcast_allocs" so we can quantify. If lazy_upcast reduces upcast_allocs by >80% and transient_scratch_peak < 400MB we're good.

sre_oncall: I'll drain the hotspots and flip the routing guard for 30m while you run tests. Keep me updated with the perf counters and error rates.

megan: Running now on staging. First run: deferred-free=32ms reduced transient peak by ~230MB, but tail latency increased 6% on some queries.

kai: Expected tradeoff. Try bumping eager_compact_threshold down a bit to avoid too-frequent compaction overhead. Maybe 64KB for small buffers.

megan: Will run that next. Also noticed kernel selector sometimes still chooses fp32 fallback even when ops could run fp16 if we set stricter kernel pref. Might add a kernel selection hint per-model that prefers quant-aware kernels.

anil: Let's not hardcode — add a model metadata flag "prefer_quant_kernels": true and let selector use that to bias scoring.

megan: Good. I'll open a PR with three changes: reduced window + eager compact tweak, lazy-upcast kv flag, selector bias flag. Will include unit tests and perf dashboards.

kai: Thanks. Once PR is up, tag me and I'll run cluster experiments. If we see memory OOMs stop in staging, promote to canary.

sre_oncall: FYI leaving monitoring on the canary path. If error rate >1.5% rollback automatically.

megan: PR link when ready. Thx all. :rocket:
